title: Asiaticoside alleviates atherosclerosis progression by suppressing RhoF-NF-kappaB/MAPK signaling and inflammation in macrophages.
authors: Wang, Junlu; Lei, Lingli; Wang, Shasha; Sun, Yuanyuan
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究积雪草苷通过RhoF降解抑制NF-kappaB/MAPK信号通路缓解动脉粥样硬化，属于药物抗炎机制研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模内容，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Asiaticoside (AT), a triterpenoid derived from Centella asiatica, has long been recognized for its anti-inflammatory properties. Its potential to ameliorate atherosclerosis (AS), a chronic inflammatory disease, positions it as a promising therapeutic agent, although its underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the anti-atherosclerotic effects of AT and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its therapeutic actions in AS. STUDY DESIGN: The research included in vivo animal experiments, in vitro cellular studies, and target exploration and validation. METHODS: High-fat diet-induced ApoE(-/-) mice were treated with AT or statins to assess AS progression, while ApoE(-/-) mice fed a chow diet served as controls. Network pharmacology and RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) of aortas identified dysregulated target genes and pathways. Oxidized low-density lipoprotein (Ox-LDL)-stimulated peritoneal macrophages were used for in vitro studies. Molecular docking, dynamics simulations, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) arrays, Western blotting (WB), immunohistochemistry (IHC), and immunofluorescence were conducted to elucidate AT's anti-inflammatory mechanisms. RESULTS: AT treatment significantly attenuated AS progression and enhanced plaque stability in the aortic roots of ApoE(-/-) mice by reducing macrophage infiltration in plaques in vivo and suppressing inflammation in ox-LDL-stimulated macrophages in vitro. Integrated network pharmacology and RNA-Seq analyses identified Ras homolog family member F (RhoF) as a key target, with significantly elevated RhoF expression in AS plaques and macrophages, which was markedly reduced by AT treatment. Mechanistically, AT bound to RhoF, promoting its proteasome-mediated degradation, which further suppressed Nuclear Factor kappa-B (NF-kappaB) and Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways, thereby inhibiting inflammation. CONCLUSION: AT mitigates AS progression and enhances plaque stability in ApoE(-/-) mice by suppressing inflammation through RhoF proteasomal degradation and inhibition of NF-kappaB/MAPK signaling pathways, highlighting its potential as an anti-atherosclerotic therapeutic agent. These effects may offer advantages over current anti-inflammatory agents, such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors, by targeting protein stability to reduce plaque rupture risk. Its promising clinical translation value warrants further exploration.
abstract_zh: 背景：积雪草苷（Asiaticoside, AT）是一种源自积雪草（Centella asiatica）的三萜类化合物，长期以来因其抗炎特性而受到认可。其改善动脉粥样硬化（atherosclerosis, AS）——一种慢性炎症性疾病——的潜力使其成为一种有前景的治疗药物，尽管其潜在机制尚未完全阐明。目的：本研究旨在评估AT的抗动脉粥样硬化作用，并阐明其在AS中治疗作用的分子机制。研究设计：研究包括体内动物实验、体外细胞研究以及靶点探索与验证。方法：高脂饮食诱导的ApoE(-/-)小鼠接受AT或他汀类药物治疗以评估AS进展，而喂食普通饮食的ApoE(-/-)小鼠作为对照。网络药理学和主动脉RNA测序（RNA-Seq）鉴定了失调的靶基因和通路。氧化低密度脂蛋白（Ox-LDL）刺激的腹膜巨噬细胞用于体外研究。采用分子对接、动力学模拟、表面等离子体共振（SPR）阵列、蛋白质印迹（WB）、免疫组织化学（IHC）和免疫荧光来阐明AT的抗炎机制。结果：AT治疗显著减轻了ApoE(-/-)小鼠主动脉根部的AS进展并增强了斑块稳定性，这是通过减少体内斑块中巨噬细胞浸润和抑制体外ox-LDL刺激的巨噬细胞炎症实现的。整合网络药理学和RNA-Seq分析将Ras同源家族成员F（RhoF）确定为一个关键靶点，AS斑块和巨噬细胞中RhoF表达显著升高，而AT治疗显著降低了其表达。机制上，AT与RhoF结合，促进其蛋白酶体介导的降解，进一步抑制核因子kappa-B（NF-kappaB）和丝裂原活化蛋白激酶（MAPK）信号通路，从而抑制炎症。结论：AT通过RhoF蛋白酶体降解和抑制NF-kappaB/MAPK信号通路来抑制炎症，从而减轻ApoE(-/-)小鼠的AS进展并增强斑块稳定性，凸显其作为抗动脉粥样硬化治疗药物的潜力。这些效应可能通过靶向蛋白质稳定性来降低斑块破裂风险，从而优于当前抗炎药物（如肿瘤坏死因子（TNF）抑制剂）。其有前景的临床转化价值值得进一步探索。
